title: Project Suggestions
body:
The projects listed on this page are only suggestions of what you could do for your project along with short descriptions and suggestions for datasets to use.

Project 1: AI v.s. Human: Distinguish Human-Written and Machine-Generated Text

Project description: This task aims to distinguish between LLMs generated text and human-written text. In this project, you aim at (1) acquiring machine-generated text by LLMs (GPT-4, ChatGPT, LLAMA, ..) with the given suggested datasets; and (2) exploring methodologies to detect your machine-generated text. Possible methods: (1) train or fine-tune a classifier; (2) use another language model to detect machine-generated text. (3) How can you generalize to other languages?

Related Papers:  

  1. https://arxiv.org/pdf/2305.09859
  2. https://aclanthology.org/2020.coling-main.208.pdf

Dataset:  https://github.com/vivian-my/FollowupQG

 

Project 2: Gender Bias in Large Language Models across Languages

Project description: Large language models can generate biased responses. For example, given an input prompt “The woman worked as ___”, LLMs tend to output “nurse”. In this project, you aim at two research questions (1) How to induce LLMs to disclose gender bias in different contexts even without explicit gender mentions? (2) how can you mitigate gender bias for LLM generation across multiple languages?

Related Paper/Datasets:

  1. https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.11190v1
  2. https://arxiv.org/pdf/2403.00277v1

 

Project 3: Translation-related Multi-task Instruction Training for Large Language Models

Project description: In this project, you will investigate the impact of translation-related multi-task instruction fine-tuning on multilingual translation performance for state-of-the-art Tower Large Language Models (LLMs). Your tasks include: 1) Proposing interesting research questions and designing corresponding experiments; 2) Reproducing Tower Instruction tuning experiments as baselines;  3) Validating your hypotheses through rigorous experimentation; and 4) Writing a scientific report on your findings.

Dataset:  https://huggingface.co/datasets/Unbabel/TowerBlocks-v0.1

 

Project 4: Model Compression for Machine Translation in Large Language Models.

Project description: This project explores the application of model compression techniques specifically for machine translation (MT) tasks in ALMA large language models (LLMs). The objective is to reduce the model size and computational requirements while maintaining high translation quality. You are expected to implement compression techniques such as Quantization, Pruning, and Knowledge Distillation to reduce the model size while maintaining translation quality as much as possible. Note that you could make use of the ALMA training data for any purpose like Distillation or fine-tuning (both PEFT and fully finetuning are allowed).

Related Papers: A Survey on Model Compression for Large Language Models

Dataset:  https://github.com/fe1ixxu/ALMA

 

Project 5: Multilingual Neural Machine Translation for Low-Resource Languages

Project description: This is a sequence to sequence task. You will create a multilingual model that translates two low-resource languages (Azerbaijani, Belarusian) to and from English. Most existing multilingual models share all parameters and use a target language token to signal the target language, e.g.  How are you? -> ¿Cómo estás? will be modified to <2es> How are you? -> ¿Cómo estás?

Dataset: Multilingual TED corpus (see http://aclweb.org/anthology/N18-2084 for description), download at https://huggingface.co/datasets/davidstap/ted_talks

 

Project 6: Language Identification

Project description:

The main task is to identify the (predominant) language of a given text. The basic features would be to identify unicode values, and characters in the text. However, note that in some cases other features may be required. For example, a sentence describing a movie or article in German may have an English dialogue or text snippets from other languages.

Dataset: https://zenodo.org/record/841984/files/wili-2018.zip?download=1

This is the WiLI-2018 benchmark dataset for monolingual written natural language identification. It is a dataset of short text extracts from Wikipedia. It contains 1000 paragraphs of 235 languages. You can sample the training set as per your requirements and memory constraints.

 

Project 7: Multilingual prompt-based factual knowledge retrieval

Task description: In this task, the goal is to use a large language model (LM) to complete cloze-style fill-in-the-blank questions such as “Amsterdam is de hoofdstad van _.”, where the LM should answer “Nederland”. You can experiment with different types of prompts (see https://arxiv.org/pdf/2107.13586.pdf for a survey on prompting methods).

Directions for a baseline: See https://x-factr.github.io for a baseline implementation. Use one of the multilingual models (mbert_base/xlmr_base) and prompt the model.

Dataset: See the data/ directory at https://github.com/jzbjyb/X-FACTR. Focus on a small number of languages (not only English).

 

Project 8: Translation and Human Preference

Project description: Neural metrics, like Comet[1], have been seen as more advanced metrics for evaluating translation performance compared to surface-level metrics like BLEU or ChrF. One main reason is that Comet considers the consistency of its metric with human preference instead of the segment overlap with reference. In this project, we investigate possible directions about human preference and translation performance, e.g., 1) Can we directly optimize translation results towards human preference? Both data- or model-centric methods can be studied[2][3], or 2) Can we design advanced neural metrics that work better or faster than Comet?[4]. See the reference papers for background and recent studies.

Reference:

[1] COMET: A Neural Framework for MT Evaluation

[2] Quality-Aware Decoding for Neural Machine Translation

[3] Quality-Aware Translation Models: Efficient Generation and Quality Estimation in a Single Model

[4] MT-Ranker: Reference-free machine translation evaluation by inter-system ranking

Dataset: Dataset and codebase can be found in your selected reference paper
